newsitem.title: USA: ADR REPORT - Gucci sags, Carlton up.
newsitem.headline: ADR REPORT - Gucci sags, Carlton up.

text.p: Gucci Group NV's American Depositary Receipts declined on Thursday, a feature in an otherwise lackluster U.S. ADR market Thursday, traders said.

Traders attributed Gucci's slip to a research note from brokerage Furman Selz that, while generally positive, noted first quarter results may face difficult comparisons against Gucci's strong sales performance in 1996.
"Furman Selz suggested this morning year-over-year comparisons will be difficult for Gucci," said a trader.
In afternoon U.S. trade, Gucci shares were off one to 72-3/8, up from an earlier low of 71-1/4.
The Furman Selz analyst was not immediately available to comment, though the analyst's assistant confirmed a research note was put out Thursday.
A second trader said the analyst said she still expects sales growth of 30 to 35 percent for the first quarter.
"Everything is sort of tentative. The one stock moving is Gucci. It was for sale this this morning and it was marked down quite sharply. That is the feature," added a third trader.

The first trader noted Gucci "is the only one of the Italian specialty group that has not corrected recently. If you look at these stocks, including Fila (Holdings SpA) and (Industrie) Natuzzi (SpA), they have come cratering down and Gucci has not, so it is a bit on the vulnerable side."
Elsewhere, Carlton Communications Plc ADRs climbed 2-1/8 to 43-1/2 after Morgan Stanley raised the stock to strong buy from outperform, the traders said.
Also, Grupo Televisa SA de CV ADRs slipped 1/4 to 26-3/8.
The company's former chairman Emilio Azcarraga Milmo died of cancer Wednesday. He stepped down as chairman in March due to ill health.
